name: Grayson Highlands
unique: Open highland balds at 5,000 feet with wild ponies grazing among granite outcrops, and the Appalachian Trail crossing Mount Rogers, Virginia's highest point.
buzz: The ponies are habituated and will investigate your lunch; the Wilburn Ridge loop is the classic. Weather changes fast and the wind is constant.

name: Arlington National Cemetery
unique: The national cemetery on the Potomac, with the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, the changing of the guard, Kennedy's grave and rows of markers on the hills.
buzz: Sobering and beautifully kept. Take the tram if you want to cover the ground, and stay for the guard change.

name: Shenandoah National Park and Skyline Drive
dates: Year round, Skyline Drive sections close for ice
unique: 105 miles of ridge road along the crest of the Blue Ridge with 75 overlooks, and 500 miles of trail through oak and hemlock forest including Hawksbill, the park's highest summit, reached from a trailhead in Page County.
buzz: The drive is the attraction and the traffic knows it. Regulars go before eight in the morning, park at Thornton Gap and walk up Stony Man instead of driving the whole road.

name: Floyd Country Store Friday Night
unique: A 1910 general store with a potbelly stove where a live old time band plays and anyone can join the flatfooting and two-step on the worn wooden floor.
buzz: Locals and visitors agree it is the most welcoming room in Appalachia; get there early for a seat and expect to be pulled into a dance.

name: Monticello
unique: Jefferson's mountaintop house with its dumbwaiters, alcove beds and clock-driven calendar, plus the reconstructed slave quarters that complicate the postcard.
buzz: The slavery exhibits get strong praise for honesty; the house tour is timed and the grounds need another hour. Book the first slot.

name: Mount Vernon
unique: George Washington's plantation on the Potomac, with the mansion, the tomb, the slave quarters, a working farm and a distillery.
buzz: The house tour and the slave memorial together tell the whole story, and the river view is beautiful. Allow three hours.

name: Virginia Museum of Fine Arts
unique: A free encyclopedic museum with Art Nouveau, African art, Faberge and a sculpture garden, plus a strong photography program.
buzz: Free and world class, with a good cafe and a sculpture garden. The Faberge collection is the surprise.

name: Luray Caverns and the Great Stalacpipe Organ
unique: A vast limestone cavern where a lithophone built into the stalactites plays music through the rock itself, the world's largest musical instrument, and it actually works.
buzz: Visitors are surprised by how good the organ recital is; the cavern is commercial but genuinely spectacular. The garden maze next door is a decent add on.

name: Marine Corps War Memorial
unique: The Iwo Jima flag raising statue in bronze, with a view across the river to the Washington monuments and a nightly sunset ceremony in summer.
buzz: The scale of the statue surprises people, and the skyline view is excellent. Free and quick.

name: Wolf Trap National Park for the Performing Arts
unique: The only national park for the performing arts, with a covered amphitheater and lawn seating under the trees, plus a barn theater for smaller shows.
buzz: Bring a picnic and a blanket for the lawn. The sound is good and the setting is hard to beat.

name: Devil's Bathtub
unique: A series of natural plunge pools carved into sandstone at the end of a creek-wading and boulder-hopping route through Jefferson National Forest.
buzz: People love it and warn the route is unmarked, slippery and not for flip-flops. Go early; it is a locals' secret that leaked.

name: American Shakespeare Center
unique: A recreation of Shakespeare's indoor Blackfriars theater, lit by chandeliers with the house lights on, where actors can see and talk to the audience.
buzz: The staging is energetic and the tickets are cheap for the quality; the town of Staunton is a good base.

name: Battleship Wisconsin
unique: An Iowa class battleship docked at Nauticus, with turrets, crew quarters and a deck you can walk, plus a science center next door.
buzz: The ship is enormous and the tour is self guided, so you can go at your pace. Good for kids.

name: Chincoteague Pony Swim
unique: Saltwater cowboys herd wild ponies across the channel at slack tide, then auction the foals to keep the herd small, a 100-year old ritual on a barrier island.
buzz: It is genuinely crowded and hot, and people still call it unforgettable. Watch from the water or a boat, not the packed shore.

name: Cumberland Gap National Historical Park
unique: The mountain pass that opened the westward trail through the Appalachians, with earthworks, a visitor center and a ridge trail across three states.
buzz: The view from the pinnacle is worth the climb, and the history is foundational. Free.

name: Frontier Culture Museum
dates: Year round, costumed interpreters most days
unique: Four working farm sites rebuilt from 17th and 18th century England, Ireland, Germany and West Africa, plus an American farmstead, spread across a valley field and staffed by interpreters who explain how each place fed the migration that filled the Shenandoah.
buzz: The West African farm and the German farm are the parts people did not expect, and the interpreters stay in role without lecturing. Plan three hours and wear walking shoes, the site is a long loop.

name: Jamestown Settlement
unique: A living history museum with replicas of the Susan Constant, a Powhatan village and a fort, telling the 1607 story.
buzz: Kids can climb the ships and try on armor, and the museum covers the hard history of the colony. Good for a family day.

name: Lewis Ginter Botanical Garden
unique: Fifty acres of themed gardens with a conservatory, a children's garden, a rose garden and a lake, plus a holiday lights show.
buzz: The conservatory is the winter win and the children's garden is genuinely good. Holiday lights sell out.

name: Maymont
unique: A 100-acre Gilded Age estate with a Romanesque mansion, Japanese and Italian gardens, and a Virginia wildlife exhibit with otters, bobcats and black bears.
buzz: Free grounds and a small mansion fee; the gardens are gorgeous in spring and the wildlife exhibits are better than expected for kids.

name: Natural Tunnel State Park
unique: A 850 foot natural tunnel carved by a creek through a mountain, with a chairlift, a train line through it and trails above.
buzz: The tunnel is genuinely dramatic and the chairlift saves the climb. Go when the train passes through.

name: University of Virginia Rotunda
unique: Jefferson's rotunda and the lawn of pavilions and student rooms, a UNESCO World Heritage site and a working university.
buzz: The lawn is the walk and the rotunda tour explains Jefferson's design. Free and central.

name: Yorktown Battlefield
unique: The battlefield where Cornwallis surrendered in 1781, with earthworks, a siege line and a driving tour through the woods.
buzz: The ranger talks make the siege make sense, and the earthworks are well preserved. Pair it with the American Revolution Museum.

name: Colonial Williamsburg
unique: Eighty-eight original and reconstructed buildings on the actual 18th century capital, with tradespeople who blacksmith, bind books and argue politics in character.
buzz: The ticket price draws complaints, but the trades and the evening programs are rated excellent. Go in spring or fall; summer heat is brutal in wool.

name: Grand Caverns
dates: Year round, spelunking trips by reservation
unique: The oldest continually operating show cave in the country, opened for tours in 1806, with shield formations found almost nowhere else and hundreds of signatures from Civil War soldiers on the walls, including a battalion roster written in candle smoke.
buzz: Guides point out the 1863 signatures and the shield formations, and the cave runs a wild caving trip for people who want to crawl instead of walk. Reviews single out the guides.

name: Barter Theatre
unique: The state theater of Virginia, founded during the Depression when actors accepted produce as admission, still producing a full season in a 1930s playhouse.
buzz: Production values are high for a small town and the history is charming; dinner on Main Street is part of the night.

name: Big Schloss Trail
company: George Washington and Jefferson National Forests
unique: A four mile round trip from the Wolf Gap saddle to a rock outcrop on the Virginia and West Virginia line, named by German settlers for a castle, with a hundred mile view and a short exposed scramble that feels bigger than the map suggests.
buzz: One of the most photographed views in the northern Valley and the reason Wolf Gap campground fills on fall weekends. The last quarter mile is a rock hop, not a trail.

name: Carter Mountain Orchard
unique: A pick your own orchard on a ridge above Charlottesville, with apple cider doughnuts, a bakery and a view of Monticello and the Blue Ridge.
buzz: The view and the doughnuts are the reason, and picking is a fall ritual. Go early on weekends.

name: Great Falls Park
unique: The Potomac compresses into a quarter mile of Class V rapids twenty minutes from the capital, with cliff-top overlooks and a boulder-strewn gorge.
buzz: Locals call it the best quick nature fix near DC; the River Trail scramble is the fun part. Parking fills by 10am on weekends.

name: Red Wing Roots Music Festival
unique: A three day roots and Americana festival in the meadow under the Natural Chimneys towers, with a bike valet, a creek for kids, camping on site and a lineup that mixes touring acts with valley bands.
buzz: People describe it as the festival that feels like a family reunion, small enough to see everything and with a reputation for treating the grounds well. Sells out most years.

name: Virginia Safari Park
unique: A 180 acre drive through safari where bison, zebra and elk stick their heads in your car, plus a walk through village with giraffes and kangaroos.
buzz: Buy the feed and accept that your car will be licked; the drive through is the fun and the walk through is a bonus. Go early.

name: Mabry Mill
unique: A water powered gristmill, sawmill and blacksmith shop on the Blue Ridge Parkway, with a millpond that reflects the whole thing and a weekend craft demonstration.
buzz: The most photographed spot on the Parkway and it earns it at dawn; the restaurant's buckwheat pancakes are a tradition.

name: Shenandoah Caverns
dates: Year round, American Celebration closes in winter
unique: The only Virginia cavern with an elevator down, and the one with bacon, strips of translucent flowstone that hang in sheets, plus a second building full of retired Rose Parade and presidential inauguration floats.
buzz: Guides point out the bacon formation first because that is what everyone photographs. The float warehouse next door surprises people more than the cave does.

name: Blue Ridge Tunnel
dates: Year round, daylight, bring a light
company: Nelson County and the City of Waynesboro
unique: A 4,273 foot railroad tunnel blasted through the Blue Ridge by hand between 1850 and 1858, abandoned for decades and reopened in 2020 as a flat gravel walk that goes from daylight into total darkness and back out the other side of the mountain.
buzz: People walk it with headlamps and describe the temperature drop and the water dripping from the ceiling. The climb back up from the west portal is the part that surprises everyone.

name: Leesburg Historic District
unique: A courthouse square of 18th and 19th century buildings, brick sidewalks, a brewery and restaurants, in the middle of Virginia wine country.
buzz: The downtown is walkable and busy on weekends, with good lunch spots and a farmers market.

name: Lexington Historic District
unique: A small Shenandoah Valley town with Washington and Lee and VMI, Stonewall Jackson's house, a historic courthouse and brick streets.
buzz: The colleges and the old houses make a compact walk, and the VMI museum is free.

name: Mill Mountain Star
unique: A 88 foot neon star on a mountain above Roanoke, with a viewpoint over the valley and the city lights at night.
buzz: The drive up is easy and the view is the payoff, especially at dusk. Free.

name: Roanoke Pinball Museum
unique: Sixty machines from the 1950s onward, all playable, in a downtown space where the volunteer mechanics will explain how a flipper works.
buzz: Everything is on free play and the collection is well maintained; a cheap hour of joy in a city that needed one.

name: Virginia Beach Boardwalk
unique: A three mile oceanfront boardwalk with restaurants, a fishing pier, a statue of Neptune and separate bike and walking lanes.
buzz: The boardwalk is wide and clean, and the Neptune statue is the photo. Busy in summer, pleasant in the off season.

name: Agecroft Hall
unique: A Tudor manor house built in England in the 1500s, dismantled, shipped across the Atlantic and rebuilt on the James River in 1925, with the original glass and oak.
buzz: The story of the move is as interesting as the house; the gardens are quiet and the tours are personal.

name: Shenandoah River Outfitters
unique: Canoe, kayak, raft and tube trips on the South Fork from a riverside base with cabins and tent sites, including a flatwater stretch that beginners can handle and a seven mile run past the Massanutten ridge.
buzz: The outfit runs shuttles all day and the staff put nervous beginners in the right boat. Tubing is slow and social in July when the river drops.

name: Virginia Museum of the Civil War at New Market
unique: The battlefield where 257 VMI cadets marched into the line in the rain in 1864 and broke it, now a museum with the flag they carried, a restored Bushong farm the fighting went through, and a walking trail over the same ground.
buzz: The cadet charge is the story everyone comes for and the museum tells it with the actual uniforms and a sound and light show. Reenactments in May draw crowds.

name: Chateau Morrisette
unique: A winery on the Blue Ridge Parkway with a tasting room, a restaurant and a lawn, making wine since the 1970s.
buzz: The setting is the sell and the restaurant is good for lunch. Check hours in winter.

name: Morven Park
unique: A 1,000 acre estate with a Greek Revival mansion, formal gardens, a carriage museum and equestrian grounds.
buzz: The carriage collection is the surprise, and the grounds are quiet. Check tour times.

name: Natural Bridge
unique: A 215-foot limestone arch that Jefferson called a wonder of the world, with a lost river, a saltpeter cave and a nightly illumination show.
buzz: People stop for an hour and stay for three; the evening light show is kitsch but charming. The walk is paved and easy.

name: Seven Bends State Park
company: Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation
customer: Paddlers, anglers, families with small kids
unique: A young state park on a seven mile serpentine stretch of the North Fork, with river access, a wade and swim beach, and bluff trails above the bends that look down on water looping back on itself.
buzz: The river access is the draw for canoeists and smallmouth anglers. Trails are easy and short, which makes it the park people bring grandparents and toddlers to.

name: Shenandoah Valley Music Festival
dates: Mid July through Labor Day weekend, weekends
customer: Couples, symphony goers, bluegrass and Americana fans
unique: Concerts on the lawn and under the pavilion at Shrine Mont, an 1870s resort of white frame hotels and cottages in a mountain hollow, with a season that mixes symphony nights, bluegrass and tribute acts in a venue that holds a few hundred people.
buzz: People bring chairs, wine and dinner and sit on the slope. The setting is the review, over and over, along with how easy it is to get close to the stage.

name: Taubman Museum of Art
unique: A free museum in a striking modern building with regional art, American painting, folk art and a sculpture gallery.
buzz: The building is the photo and the collection is free. Good rainy day stop.

name: Virginia Scenic Railway
dates: Selected days year round, fall color and holiday runs sell out
unique: Excursions from the 1902 Staunton depot, east through the Blue Ridge Tunnel on the active Norfolk Southern line or west along the Cowpasture River, with onboard dining in a restored car and a route no highway can match.
buzz: The eastbound run through the tunnel is the one people book first. Reviews praise the crew and the view from the dome seats and warn that the trip is about the ride, not the destination.

name: Massanutten Resort
customer: Families, skiers from DC, mountain bikers, golfers
unique: A 6,000 acre four season mountain with southern Virginia's largest ski hill, an indoor and outdoor waterpark, a lift served bike park and a summer adventure course, all on one ridge above the valley.
buzz: The waterpark is what sells it to families, the ski hill is small but close, and the bike trails have a serious following. Reviews warn about condo quality varying by unit.

name: Natural Chimneys Park
unique: Seven limestone towers up to 120 feet high left standing where a cave roof collapsed, in a county park with a campground, a pool and a creek, on the site of a resort that has drawn valley visitors since the 1800s.
buzz: Small enough to walk in ten minutes and strange enough to keep people an hour. The festival grounds beside the towers host the county's biggest music weekend each June.

name: Bryce Resort
dates: Year round, ski December–March, bike park April–November
customer: Beginner skiers, mountain bikers, families from DC
unique: A small four season mountain two hours from Washington with the state's most forgiving beginner slopes, a lift served bike park with jump lines, and a summer tubing hill, all in a valley with no other ski area within a hundred miles.
buzz: People describe it as where you learn to ski without paying resort prices, and the bike park has become the reason younger visitors come in summer. Lines are short, terrain is modest.

name: Sherando Lake Recreation Area
company: George Washington and Jefferson National Forests
customer: Families, swimmers, campers from the valley
unique: A spring fed mountain lake built by the CCC at the foot of the Blue Ridge with a sandy beach, a roped swim area, a second smaller lake for fishing, and trails that climb straight up into the national forest.
buzz: The beach fills by ten on July weekends and locals go on weekdays. Campground books out early and the water stays cold even in August.

name: Sunspots Studios
cost: Free to watch, classes $60 and up
dates: Year round, demos most days until mid afternoon
customer: Craft curious, families, people buying gifts
unique: A working hot shop downtown where four glassblowers rotate through live demonstrations all day, with a gallery of their work and classes that put you at the bench making a paperweight or ornament.
buzz: The demo is free and people stay for two or three rounds of it. The beginner glass class is the birthday and anniversary booking in town.

name: Woodrow Wilson Presidential Library and Museum
unique: The manse where Wilson was born in 1856, with the family's furniture in place, a museum on his presidency and the League of Nations fight, a World War One trench exhibit, and the Pierce-Arrow limousine that carried him to his inauguration.
buzz: The trench recreation and the stroke story are what visitors remember. Some find the presentation old fashioned, and the docents are the ones who bring it alive.

name: Rockingham County Fair
customer: Farm families, teens, demolition derby crowds
unique: Virginia's largest county fair, running six days of livestock shows, a rodeo, truck and tractor pulls and a demolition derby at a permanent fairground south of Harrisonburg, with the state's biggest 4-H presence.
buzz: Locals treat it as the end of summer. The derby and the rodeo sell out the grandstand, and the livestock barns are full of kids who have been showing since they could walk.

name: Woodstock Tower
dates: Year round, forest road may close in winter
company: George Washington and Jefferson National Forests
unique: A forest service lookout tower at the end of a short climb above the town, looking down on the seven bends of the Shenandoah and across to the Massanutten range, built by the CCC and reachable by car with a two mile walk if the gate is open.
buzz: Locals send visitors here instead of the national park because the view of the river bends is better and there is no entrance fee. Sunset is the time.

name: Elizabeth Furnace Recreation Area
company: George Washington and Jefferson National Forests
unique: The stone stack of an 1836 iron furnace that ran on slave and immigrant labor and cast stoves and kettles until the 1880s, standing beside a creek swimming hole and a picnic ground in a valley reached by one road over the mountain.
buzz: The furnace stack is a five minute walk and kids end up in the creek behind it. Campers use it as a base for the Massanutten trails.

name: Green Valley Book Fair
dates: Six events a year, roughly ten days each
unique: A 30,000 square foot warehouse south of Harrisonburg stacked with hundreds of thousands of publisher overstock books at a fraction of cover price, open only a few weeks a year and drawing people from several states on opening day.
buzz: People bring boxes and a list. The schedule is posted a year ahead because regulars plan trips around it, and the children's section is where the damage gets done.

name: Kline's Dairy Bar
customer: Students, families, anyone in line after a ball game
unique: Frozen custard made fresh daily since 1943 in a walk-up window downtown, with a flavor of the week that people check online and a chalkboard that has launched arguments about black raspberry versus vanilla.
buzz: The line at night is the institution. Locals order a small and get a mountain, and the flavor of the week is a genuine topic of conversation in town.

name: Wayne Theatre
dates: Year round, season runs fall to spring
customer: Theatre goers, touring band fans, families at holiday shows
unique: A 1926 vaudeville and movie house on Main Street, restored after decades dark, with a small balcony, an art gallery in the lobby and a season of touring concerts, plays and classic films that a town of 22,000 should not be able to support.
buzz: The restoration is the story locals tell, and the acoustics in a house that size are why touring acts stop. Film nights and the holiday musical sell out.

name: Beverley Historic District
unique: A downtown grid of brick sidewalks and 19th century storefronts with cast iron porches, a 1901 opera house and a courthouse by Thomas Jefferson's firm, dense enough to cover on foot in an afternoon and used as a film set for period pictures.
buzz: Architectural Digest put it among the best main streets in the country and locals quote that. The farmer's market and the bookshops keep it from feeling like a museum.

name: Luray Zoo, a Rescue Zoo
unique: A small private zoo built entirely around surrendered and confiscated animals, with a reptile house, big cats and primates that came from the pet trade, and signs that explain why the animals are there rather than just naming them.
buzz: It is honest about being a rescue rather than a showcase, and visitors say the staff will talk for twenty minutes about an individual animal's history. Not a polished attraction, and better for it.

name: Shenandoah County Fair
customer: Local families, harness racing fans, livestock exhibitors
unique: One of the oldest county fairs in the state, with a half mile harness racing track that still runs live meets, plus the usual 4-H barns, tractor pull and a grandstand that has been rebuilt around the same oval.
buzz: The harness races are the thing outsiders do not expect. Regulars come for the track and the livestock, and the fair still feels like a county event rather than a carnival.

name: Staunton Braves at Gypsy Hill Park
customer: Families, baseball people, summer night crowds
unique: Summer collegiate baseball in a 1930s WPA stone stadium inside a 214 acre city park, where the players stay with host families and the crowd sits close enough to hear the infield talk, with a pool and a miniature train in the same park.
buzz: Cheap tickets, real baseball and a small grandstand that fills on fireworks nights. Locals bring chairs to the berm and let kids run.

name: The Dayton Market
customer: Food shoppers, furniture hunters, Mennonite country visitors
unique: A big indoor market where Old Order Mennonite families sell hand built oak furniture, quilts, canned goods, fry pies and still warm apple pie from stalls they run themselves, in a barn-like building on the edge of Dayton.
buzz: The fry pies and the deli counter draw people from Harrisonburg weekly. Furniture buyers come with truck measurements and leave with a table.

name: Augusta County Fair
customer: Farm families, livestock exhibitors, ride crowds
unique: One of the oldest county fairs in Virginia, running since the 1860s at the Augusta Expo grounds, with beef and dairy shows, a tractor pull, harness racing history in the grandstand and a midway that still fits on one gravel lot.
buzz: The livestock barns are the real event and the exhibitors have been coming for generations. Fairgoers say it is smaller than Rockingham's and easier to walk.

name: Edinburg Mill
dates: Year round, restaurant closed early in the week
unique: A four story 1848 grist mill that survived Sheridan's burning of the valley, now a museum of milling and valley farm life with the original machinery in place and a restaurant in the mill room.
buzz: The volunteers know the mill's escape from the 1864 fire in detail. Visitors come for the building and stay for the exhibits on how flour got made.

name: Page Valley Fair
customer: Local families, demolition derby crowds, livestock people
unique: A county fair that still runs on 4-H livestock shows, a tractor pull and a demolition derby in front of the Blue Ridge, now in its seventies and small enough that the same families have been showing animals for three generations.
buzz: The derby fills the grandstand and the fair food is the fair food. Locals say it is the week the county actually turns out.

name: White Oak Lavender Farm
dates: May–August peak bloom, grounds open spring–fall
unique: Eight thousand lavender plants on a working farm with a distillation shed, a u-pick field in June and July, and a tasting room for lavender lemonade and wine from the vineyard next door, run by a family that started with a hobby row.
buzz: The bloom window is short and people plan around it. The distillation demo and the animals in the barn keep kids occupied while adults sit on the porch.

name: Wright's Dairy Rite
customer: Local families, car clubs, milkshake people
unique: A drive-in with carhop service on a curved canopy, serving burgers and milkshakes to cars parked in the same spots since the 1950s, with the original neon sign still standing over Greenville Avenue.
buzz: The carhops still come to the window and the milkshakes are the order. It is the stop people show visitors when they want to prove Staunton is not all Shakespeare.

name: Explore More Discovery Museum
unique: A hands-on children's museum downtown with a full sized ambulance, a bank vault, a television studio and a maker space, built into two floors of a former department store.
buzz: Parents say it buys three hours on a rainy day and the staff keep the exhibits working, which is not universal in children's museums.

name: Luray Carillon Singing Tower
dates: Recitals spring through fall, tower grounds year round
company: Town of Luray and Luray Caverns
customer: Music people, couples, anyone parked in town
unique: A 117 foot stone tower holding a 47 bell carillon, donated by the Luray Caverns family and played in free outdoor recitals that you listen to from the lawn, one of the few carillons in the country a passerby can walk up to.
buzz: People stumble onto a recital without knowing the tower existed and stay for the whole thing. The bells carry across the whole town.

name: Route 11 Potato Chips
dates: Monday–Saturday, weekday mornings best for frying
unique: A kettle chip plant with a viewing gallery where you watch a batch go from sliced potatoes to bagged chips, and a counter selling warm chips and flavors that never make it to grocery shelves.
buzz: Everyone says to go on a weekday morning when the fryer is running. The salt and vinegar and the Mama Zuma's Revenge are the ones people carry out by the case.

name: Virginia Quilt Museum
unique: Three floors of rotating exhibitions in an 1850s mill building, covering everything from 19th century album quilts to contemporary art quilts, with the state's best collection of documented Virginia-made bedcovers.
buzz: Quilters come from out of state for the exhibitions and the staff will explain the pattern and the dating. Non-quilters are surprised by how much of it reads as painting.

name: Augusta Stone Church
dates: Grounds year round, church open for services and by arrangement
unique: A stone meeting house built in 1749 and still in use, the oldest church west of the Blue Ridge in continuous service, with the original walls, galleries and graveyard full of German and Scotch-Irish settlers who came down the valley road.
buzz: Visitors come for the graveyard and the hand cut stone. Services still happen here, which is the part people find hard to believe.

name: Bridgewater Lawn Party
customer: Local families, engine collectors, carnival crowds
unique: A fire company fundraiser that turned into four days of steam and gas engines, antique tractors, a carnival midway and food stands on the Oakdale grounds, running since the 1930s and still staffed by volunteers.
buzz: The engine show is the part outsiders do not know about. Locals go every night of it, and the fire company still keeps the money.

name: Camera Heritage Museum
unique: Over two thousand cameras packed into a downtown storefront, from wooden plate cameras and spy cameras to the first Leicas and Polaroids, collected by a camera repairman who will take one apart in front of you.
buzz: Visitors call it a hoard in the best sense and say the owner talks them through the mechanics of anything they point at. It closed for a while and is open again.

name: Edith J. Carrier Arboretum
customer: Walkers, birders, students, parents with strollers
unique: A 125 acre woodland arboretum on the James Madison campus with labeled tree collections, a native plant trail, a pond and a boardwalk, free and open to the public every day.
buzz: Used by locals as a quiet walking loop and by birders during migration. The azalea and rhododendron bloom in spring is the busiest week.

name: Hupp's Hill Civil War Park
customer: Civil War students, families, I-81 travelers
unique: A wooded hill above Strasburg where Confederate earthworks are still cut into the ground and a small museum holds artifacts dug from the battlefield, on the site of a signal station used in the 1864 valley campaign.
buzz: A quiet free stop with original trenches you can walk through. The museum is small and the volunteers are the ones who make it worth the detour.

name: The Art Space on 211
dates: Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday afternoons, or by chance
customer: Art browsers, people escaping a rainy cavern day
unique: A rambling gallery in a converted building on Route 211 showing dozens of valley artists and craftspeople at once, from plein air painters to potters to furniture makers, with the artists often sitting the desk.
buzz: Long time Luray stop that changed its name from the Warehouse Art Gallery and moved up the highway. Visitors describe it as bigger inside than it looks and full of things priced for actual houses.

name: Cooter's Place in Luray
dates: Year round, closed some weekdays in winter
customer: Dukes of Hazzard fans, roadside collectors, kids
unique: Ben Jones, the actor who played Cooter, keeps a free museum of the television show here: the General Lee, the tow truck, costumes and a replica garage, moved over the mountain from Sperryville to a bigger building on Route 211.
buzz: Free admission and unapologetically devoted to one 1980s show. Fans spend an hour, everyone else takes fifteen minutes and photographs the car.

name: Rocktown History
customer: Genealogists, local history people, rainy day families
unique: The county historical society's museum and research library in Dayton, with Civil War collections, valley furniture, a genealogy room that draws people from other states, and exhibits on the Mennonite and German settlement of the Shenandoah.
buzz: The genealogy volunteers are the reason people drive in. The museum side is compact and the bookstore is well stocked on local titles.

name: Waynesboro Street Arts Trail
unique: A self guided walk past a dozen large murals and painted utility boxes through downtown and along the South River, with a map that ties each piece to the artist and the building it is on.
buzz: A free hour that has turned a quiet Main Street into something people photograph. The river greenway section is the pleasant surprise.

name: Meems Bottom Covered Bridge
unique: A 204 foot single span over the North Fork, the longest remaining covered bridge in Virginia, burned by arson in 1976 and rebuilt by the county, still carrying a rural road across the river.
buzz: A five minute stop that photographers stretch to half an hour. The truss structure inside is visible from the roadway and the river shallows below are a wading spot in summer.

name: Shenandoah Valley Art Center
customer: Art browsers, gift shoppers, local artists
unique: A nonprofit community art center in a Main Street building with changing exhibitions by valley artists, working studios, and classes in clay, painting and printmaking open to anyone who signs up.
buzz: Small, free and genuinely local, with shows that rotate often enough that regulars stop in monthly. The gift shop is where people buy valley made pottery.

name: The Russell Museum
customer: Outsider art fans, seekers, the incurably curious
unique: The painted canvases and sculpted figures of Walter Russell, a early 20th century sculptor and self taught cosmologist who wrote about light and consciousness, kept in a small museum run by the philosophical university he founded in this valley town.
buzz: A strange and sincere place that most visitors had never heard of. People either find it profound or walk through in fifteen minutes, and both reviews exist.
